fichas.title: Preventative fire protection
fichas.summary: Preventative fire protection comprises construction, technical and organisational measures. Construction measures address escape routes, stairwells, fire compartments, building components and fire-protection installations. Technical measures include automatic detection, sprinklers and smoke and heat extraction. Organisational measures include appointing a fire-protection representative and preparing fire-safety arrangements and plans. Regulations cited include DIN 4102, DIN EN 13501, MBO, LBO and other specialist provisions.
uses: Prevent fires and limit the spread of fire and smoke
Enable rescue of people and animals and effective firefighting
Guide construction, technical systems and fire-safety organisation

fichas.title: Escape routes and legally essential stairwells
fichas.summary: Residential or commercial units with at least one occupied room require two independent escape routes to the open air on each storey. Depending on the building and route, escape may be via legally essential stairs, a second stair, or a location accessible to fire-brigade rescue equipment. A safety stairwell can remove the need for a second escape route when protected from fire and smoke. The page diagrams theoretical escape arrangements and notes special fire-protection requirements for staircases, stairwells and corridors.
uses: Provide independent routes for escape and rescue
Connect occupied rooms to stairwells or the open air

dimensions.label: Maximum distance to an exit
dimensions.context: From every location in an occupied room, at least one exit into a legally essential stairwell or into the open air must be within this distance.
dimensions.ocr_raw: From every location in an occupied room, there must be within max. 35 m at least one exit into a legally essential stairwell or into the open air
